Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning of al-Taghiyah according to the lexicographers is their transgression. And the form "fa'ilah" may come with the meaning of verbal nouns, such as 'aqibah and 'afiyah.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Do you see for them any remnant?﴾ There are three opinions concerning it.

The first: "min baqa'" (of survival), said by al-Farra'.

The second: "min baqiyah" (of remainder), said by Abu 'Ubaydah. He said: it is a verbal noun like "al-taghiyah."

[p. 349] Allah's words: ﴿And when the Trumpet is blown with a single blast﴾. On this there are two opinions.

One is that it is the first blast. This is the view of 'Ata'.

The second is that it is the last blast. This is the view of Ibn al-Sa'ib and Muqatil. ﴿And the earth and the mountains are lifted﴾, meaning the earth and the mountains and what is on them are lifted up. ﴿Then they are crushed with a single crushing﴾, meaning they are broken and pounded with one blow, without a second, until they become level, with nothing on them, and become like a stretched hide. We have already pointed to this meaning in [Surat al-A'raf], at His words: ﴿He made it into dust﴾ [7:143]. Al-Farra' said: He said fa-dukkatā (they were crushed, dual) and did not say fa-dukkikna (they were crushed, feminine plural), because He treated the mountains as one thing, like His words: ﴿that the heavens and the earth were joined together﴾ [21:30]. They recited a line of poetry:

"They are both our lords, claiming it, but they lead us only in that their two flocks have given birth (or readied for birth)."

The Arabs say: qad yassarati al-ghanam (the sheep have given birth), when they have given birth or made ready for birth.

Allah's words: ﴿So on that Day the Event will occur﴾, meaning the Resurrection will be established. ﴿And the sky will be split open﴾ because of the descent of those in it of the angels. ﴿And it will be frail on that Day﴾. On this there are two opinions.

One is that its frailty is its weakness and its tearing apart from fear. This is the view of Muqatil.

The second is that it is its splitting. This is the view of al-Farra'. ﴿And the angels﴾, meaning the angels, and it is a collective noun. ﴿Will be on its edges﴾, meaning on its sides. Al-Zajjaj said: The raja' (edge) of anything is its side, and it is a maqsur (a noun with a final alif). Its dual is rajawan, and its plural is arja'. Most of the exegetes hold that what is referred to is the sky. Al-Dahhak said: When the sky is split open, the angels will be on its rim until Allah commands them, and they will descend to the earth and surround it and those upon it. It is reported from Sa'id ibn Jubayr that he said: on the edges of this world.

Allah's words: ﴿And above them, on that Day, will bear the Throne of your Lord eight﴾. On this there are three opinions.

One is: above their heads, meaning the Throne is upon the heads of the bearers. This is the view of Muqatil.

The second is: above those who are on its edges, meaning the bearers of the Throne are above the angels who are on its edges.

The third is: that they are above the people of the Resurrection. Al-Mawardi related these two. "On that Day" means the Day of Resurrection. "Eight" has three opinions.

One is: eight angels. A hadith (report) came: "Today they are four, and when the Day of Resurrection comes, Allah will reinforce them with four other angels." This is the view of the majority.

The second is: eight rows of angels, whose number none knows but Allah the Mighty and Majestic. This is the view of Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn Jubayr, and 'Ikrima.

[p. 351] The third is: eight parts of the Karubiyyun, whose number none knows but Allah. This is the view of Muqatil. Abu Dawud has related in his Sunan from the hadith of Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "I have been permitted to narrate about an angel of Allah's angels, one of the bearers of the Throne: that the distance between the lobe of his ear and his shoulder is a journey of seven hundred years."

Allah's words: ﴿On that Day you will be presented﴾ before Allah for your reckoning, (nothing) is hidden from Him. Hamza and al-Kisa'i recited la yakhfā (it will not be hidden) with the ya'. The rest recited it with the ta'. The meaning is: nothing will be hidden from Him ﴿of you, any hidden thing﴾, meaning any hidden soul or any hidden deed. In the hadith of Abu Musa from the Prophet (ﷺ), he said: "People will be presented on the Day of Resurrection three presentations. As for two of them, there will be disputing and excuses. As for the third, then the pages will fly in the hands, so one takes his in his right hand and one takes his in his left." 'Umar ibn al-Khattab used to say: Take account of yourselves before you are brought to account, weigh yourselves before you are weighed, and adorn yourselves for the Greatest Presentation, on that Day none of you will be hidden, ﴿no hidden thing of you will be concealed﴾.

Allah's words: ﴿Then he will say: "Here, read my book!"﴾ Al-Zajjaj said: hā'um (here, take) is an imperative addressed to a group, equivalent to hākum. You say to one man: hā yā rajul; to two: hā'umā yā rajulān; to three or more: hā'um yā rijāl.

[p. 352] The exegetes said: He says this out of confidence in his safety and joy at his salvation. Muqatil mentioned that it was revealed concerning Abu Salama ibn 'Abd al-Asad.

Allah's words: ﴿Indeed, I thought﴾, meaning I knew and was certain in the world, ﴿that I would meet my account﴾, meaning that I would be raised and reckoned in the Hereafter. ﴿So he will be in a pleasing life﴾, meaning a state of life ﴿well-pleasing﴾. Al-Farra' said: meaning in it there is contentment. Al-Zajjaj said: meaning one that has contentment, which those who live in it find pleasing. Abu 'Ubayda said: its figurative sense is that of marḍiyya (pleased with). ﴿In an elevated Garden﴾, meaning of elevated dwellings, ﴿its fruits within reach﴾, meaning its fruits are near, ﴿hanging low﴾, meaning close to whoever reaches for them. Qutuf is the plural of qiṭf, which is what is plucked from fruits. Al-Bara' ibn 'Azib said: he reaches for the fruit while lying down.

Allah's words: ﴿Eat﴾, meaning it will be said to them: Eat ﴿and drink with satisfaction for what you advanced﴾, meaning what you sent ahead of good deeds ﴿in the past days﴾, which are the days of the world. ﴿But as for he who is given his record in his left hand﴾. Muqatil said: It was revealed concerning al-Aswad ibn 'Abd al-Aswad, whom Hamza killed at Badr, and he was the brother of Abu Salama. It was also said: it was revealed concerning Abu Jahl.

Allah's words: ﴿He will say, "Oh, I wish I had not been given my record"﴾, because of what he sees in it of ugly deeds, ﴿and I had not known what my account is!﴾, because there is no benefit for him in that reckoning; all of it is against him. Ibn Mas'ud, Qatada, and Ya'qub would drop the ha' from kitābiyah and ḥisābiyah in continuous recitation. Al-Zajjaj said: The correct practice is to pause on these ha's and not to join them, because they were added for pausing. Some people drop them in continuous recitation, but I do not like to oppose the mushaf (the written codex). Likewise is His words: ﴿And what will make you know what it is?﴾ [101:10].

Allah's words: ﴿Oh, I wish it had been the end!﴾, meaning the death he died in the world, ﴿it was the decisive one﴾ [p. 353], meaning the one that cut off life. It is as if he wishes for the permanence of death, and that he had not been raised for reckoning. ﴿My authority has perished from me﴾. On this there are two opinions.

One is: my proof has been lost to me. This is the view of Mujahid, 'Ikrima, al-Dahhak, and al-Suddi.

The second is: my dominion has left me. This is the view of Ibn Zayd.

Allah's words: ﴿Seize him﴾, meaning Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Seize him and shackle him﴾, meaning gather his hand to his neck, ﴿then burn him in Hell﴾, meaning put him into the Fire. Al-Zajjaj said: make him roast in the Fire. ﴿Then bind him in a chain﴾, which consists of linked rings, ﴿whose length is seventy cubits﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: by the cubit of the king. Nawf al-Shami said: each cubit is seventy spans, and the span is farther than the distance between you and Mecca; and it was in the courtyard of Kufa. Sufyan said: each cubit is seventy cubits. Abu Dawud has related in his Sunan from the hadith of Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "I have been permitted to narrate about an angel of Allah's angels, one of the bearers of the Throne: that the distance between the lobe of his ear and his shoulder is a journey of seven hundred years."

Allah's words: ﴿On that Day you will be presented﴾ before Allah for your reckoning, (nothing) is hidden from Him. Hamza and al-Kisa'i recited la yakhfā (it will not be hidden) with the ya'. The rest recited it with the ta'. The meaning is: nothing will be hidden from Him ﴿of you, any hidden thing﴾, meaning any hidden soul or any hidden deed. In the hadith of Abu Musa from the Prophet (ﷺ), he said: "People will be presented on the Day of Resurrection three presentations. As for two of them, there will be disputing and excuses. As for the third, then the pages will fly in the hands, so one takes his in his right hand and one takes his in his left." 'Umar ibn al-Khattab used to say: Take account of yourselves before you are brought to account, weigh yourselves before you are weighed, and adorn yourselves for the Greatest Presentation, on that Day none of you will be hidden, ﴿no hidden thing of you will be concealed﴾.

Allah's words: ﴿Then he will say: "Here, read my book!"﴾ Al-Zajjaj said: hā'um (here, take) is an imperative addressed to a group, equivalent to hākum. You say to one man: hā yā rajul; to two: hā'umā yā rajulān; to three or more: hā'um yā rijāl.

[p. 352] The exegetes said: He says this out of confidence in his safety and joy at his salvation. Muqatil mentioned that it was revealed concerning Abu Salama ibn 'Abd al-Asad.

Allah's words: ﴿Indeed, I thought﴾, meaning I knew and was certain in the world, ﴿that I would meet my account﴾, meaning that I would be raised and reckoned in the Hereafter. ﴿So he will be in a pleasing life﴾, meaning a state of life ﴿well-pleasing﴾. Al-Farra' said: meaning in it there is contentment. Al-Zajjaj said: meaning one that has contentment, which those who live in it find pleasing. Abu 'Ubayda said: its figurative sense is that of marḍiyya (pleased with). ﴿In an elevated Garden﴾, meaning of elevated dwellings, ﴿its fruits within reach﴾, meaning its fruits are near, ﴿hanging low﴾, meaning close to whoever reaches for them. Qutuf is the plural of qiṭf, which is what is plucked from fruits. Al-Bara' ibn 'Azib said: he reaches for the fruit while lying down.

Allah's words: ﴿Eat﴾, meaning it will be said to them: Eat ﴿and drink with satisfaction for what you advanced﴾, meaning what you sent ahead of good deeds ﴿in the past days﴾, which are the days of the world. ﴿But as for he who is given his record in his left hand﴾. Muqatil said: It was revealed concerning al-Aswad ibn 'Abd al-Aswad, whom Hamza killed at Badr, and he was the brother of Abu Salama. It was also said: it was revealed concerning Abu Jahl.

Allah's words: ﴿He will say, "Oh, I wish I had not been given my record"﴾, because of what he sees in it of ugly deeds, ﴿and I had not known what my account is!﴾, because there is no benefit for him in that reckoning; all of it is against him. Ibn Mas'ud, Qatada, and Ya'qub would drop the ha' from kitābiyah and ḥisābiyah in continuous recitation. Al-Zajjaj said: The correct practice is to pause on these ha's and not to join them, because they were added for pausing. Some people drop them in continuous recitation, but I do not like to oppose the mushaf (the written codex). Likewise is His words: ﴿And what will make you know what it is?﴾ [101:10].

Allah's words: ﴿Oh, I wish it had been the end!﴾, meaning the death he died in the world, ﴿it was the decisive one﴾ [p. 353], meaning the one that cut off life. It is as if he wishes for the permanence of death, and that he had not been raised for reckoning. ﴿My authority has perished from me﴾. On this there are two opinions.

One is: my proof has been lost to me. This is the view of Mujahid, 'Ikrima, al-Dahhak, and al-Suddi.

The second is: my dominion has left me. This is the view of Ibn Zayd.

Allah's words: ﴿Seize him﴾, meaning Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Seize him and shackle him﴾, meaning gather his hand to his neck, ﴿then burn him in Hell﴾, meaning put him into the Fire. Al-Zajjaj said: make him roast in the Fire. ﴿Then bind him in a chain﴾, which consists of linked rings, ﴿whose length is seventy cubits﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: by the cubit of the king. Nawf al-Shami said: each cubit is seventy spans, and the span is farther than the distance between you and Mecca; and it was in the courtyard of Kufa. Sufyan said: each cubit is seventy cubits. Muqatil said: its length is seventy cubits by the first cubit. It is said that all the people of the Fire are in that chain.

Allah's words: ﴿Then thread him﴾, meaning insert him. Al-Farra' said: It is mentioned that it enters through the rear of the disbeliever and comes out from his head, and that is his threading on it. The meaning is: then thread the chain through him. But the Arabs say: "I put my head into the cap" and "I put it into my head." It is also said: "The ring does not enter my hand; rather the hand enters the ring." They permitted this usage because its meaning is well known.

Allah's words: ﴿Indeed, he did not believe in Allah the Great﴾, meaning he did not affirm His oneness and greatness, ﴿and did not encourage the feeding of the needy﴾, meaning he did not feed him, nor did he command feeding him [p. 354]. ﴿So today he has no sympathetic friend here﴾, meaning a relative who would benefit him, that is, one who would intercede for him, ﴿nor any food except from ghislin﴾. On this there are three opinions.

One is that it is the pus of the people of the Fire. This is the view of Ibn 'Abbas. Muqatil said: when the pus and blood flow, they hasten to eat it before the Fire eats it.

The second is: a tree which the people of the Fire eat. This is the view of al-Dahhak and al-Rabi'.

The third is: that it is the washings of their bowels. This is the view of Yahya ibn Sallam. Ibn Qutayba said: it is fi'lin from "ghasaltu" (I washed), as if it were a washing.

Allah's words: ﴿except the wrongdoers﴾, meaning the disbelievers.

[p. 349] Allah's words: ﴿And when the Trumpet is blown with a single blast﴾. On this there are two opinions.

One is that it is the first blast. This is the view of 'Ata'.

The second is that it is the last blast. This is the view of Ibn al-Sa'ib and Muqatil. ﴿And the earth and the mountains are lifted﴾, meaning the earth and the mountains and what is on them are lifted up. ﴿Then they are crushed with a single crushing﴾, meaning they are broken and pounded with one blow, without a second, until they become level, with nothing on them, and become like a stretched hide. We have already pointed to this meaning in [Surat al-A'raf], at His words: ﴿He made it into dust﴾ [7:143]. Al-Farra' said: He said fa-dukkatā (they were crushed, dual) and did not say fa-dukkikna (they were crushed, feminine plural), because He treated the mountains as one thing, like His words: ﴿that the heavens and the earth were joined together﴾ [21:30]. They recited a line of poetry:

"They are both our lords, claiming it, but they lead us only in that their two flocks have given birth (or readied for birth)."

The Arabs say: qad yassarati al-ghanam (the sheep have given birth), when they have given birth or made ready for birth.

Allah's words: ﴿So on that Day the Event will occur﴾, meaning the Resurrection will be established. ﴿And the sky will be split open﴾ because of the descent of those in it of the angels. ﴿And it will be frail on that Day﴾. On this there are two opinions.

One is that its frailty is its weakness and its tearing apart from fear. This is the view of Muqatil.

The second is that it is its splitting. This is the view of al-Farra'. ﴿And the angels﴾, meaning the angels, and it is a collective noun. ﴿Will be on its edges﴾, meaning on its sides. Al-Zajjaj said: The raja' (edge) of anything is its side, and it is a maqsur (a noun with a final alif). Its dual is rajawan, and its plural is arja'. Most of the exegetes hold that what is referred to is the sky. Al-Dahhak said: When the sky is split open, the angels will be on its rim until Allah commands them, and they will descend to the earth and surround it and those upon it. It is reported from Sa'id ibn Jubayr that he said: on the edges of this world.

Allah's words: ﴿And above them, on that Day, will bear the Throne of your Lord eight﴾. On this there are three opinions.

One is: above their heads, meaning the Throne is upon the heads of the bearers. This is the view of Muqatil.

The second is: above those who are on its edges, meaning the bearers of the Throne are above the angels who are on its edges.

The third is: that they are above the people of the Resurrection. Al-Mawardi related these two. "On that Day" means the Day of Resurrection. "Eight" has three opinions.

One is: eight angels. A hadith (report) came: "Today they are four, and when the Day of Resurrection comes, Allah will reinforce them with four other angels." This is the view of the majority.

The second is: eight rows of angels, whose number none knows but Allah the Mighty and Majestic. This is the view of Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn Jubayr, and 'Ikrima.

[p. 351] The third is: eight parts of the Karubiyyun, whose number none knows but Allah. This is the view of Muqatil. Its saying, exalted is He: ﴿So I swear not﴾. "Lā" (no) is a rejection of the words of the polytheists, as if it were said: the matter is not as the polytheists say. ﴿I swear by what you see﴾ ﴿and what you do not see﴾. Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 69, verse 44–52:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And if he had invented against Us some [false] sayings﴾, meaning: if Muhammad had undertaken to say about Us what We had not said, ﴿We would have seized him by the right hand﴾, meaning: We would have seized him with power and might. This was said by al-Farra' (a grammarian of Kufa), al-Mubarrad, and al-Zajjaj (a grammarian and Qur'an scholar).
